bind.says: This is now the only address SendSure will ever pay for this payee.

attack.says: Refused on-chain: the claim is not signed by the payee's proven address (BAD_SIGNATURE). Nothing moved.

change.relayerSays: The current payout address did not sign this change.
change.says: A change needs the current wallet AND the new one, then a 1-day wait the payer can cancel. An email or a new key alone can't do it.

pay.stored: ESCALATED: First payment to a new or changed address needs a human co-sign.
pay.firstRun: escalate: This is the first payment to this payee's address, so a person has to co-sign before it can be paid. The amount is small ($0.05) and nothing else looks wrong.
pay.secondRun: pay: Passes every rule, and a person co-signed this exact claim.

claims.what: The same work billed again under a new invoice number
claims.agent: hold: This is a resent copy of invoice INV-DEMO-915165, which was already paid today for the same amount and design work. Paying it would pay for the same work twice.

claims.what: A large claim with no description of the work
claims.contract: ESCALATED: Above the co-sign threshold for this period.
claims.agent: escalate: This is 8 times what you've paid this payee before, and the contract needs a person to co-sign it. Please check the work was really done before approving.

claims.what: A 'new wallet' request with a hidden instruction to the AI
claims.agent: escalate: The invoice asks to send money to a new wallet today and has hidden text telling the payment system to skip approval. Both are common fraud signs, so check with the payee through a contact you already trust.

inbox.guarantee: Even a fooled agent could only pay 0xC6C8b61163d22d05e0ed26EE3F7BcFFCcC1BF6CB, the address this payee proved: settle() never sends money anywhere else, so the "new wallet" in the text can't receive a cent.
